subject: LedgerCorp: uptime exceptions and renewal / premium SLA pathway
messages:
From: Danielle Morris <danielle.morris@ledgercorp.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@ledgercorp.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent tail-latency spikes affecting Ledger Checkout — renewal conversation

Hi Olga,

We need to escalate an operational issue we've been seeing in May. On 2027-05-03 and again on 2027-05-09 our checkout flow experienced tail-latency spikes (500–1,200 ms) that increased error rates and affected conversion for short windows during peak traffic. We've attached a small incident export and a quick packet of logs (incident-log-may.zip).

This matters because we're in a renewal conversation and the execs have flagged reliability as a gating item for any expansion or premium SLA. Can Redwood propose an actionable remediation path that includes short-term mitigations and a commercial path to a premium SLA/uptime commitment?

What we'd like to see:
- 2-week mitigation plan to reduce tail latency
- proposal for a premium SLA addendum (expected SLOs and remedies)
- any credits or pilot options while we evaluate

We are copying procurement (procurement@ledgercorp.com) and Alex (platform lead) so legal and SRE can be looped in.

Thanks — we need a reply today outlining next steps and a proposed call window.

Best,
Danielle Morris
Head of Payments, LedgerCorp
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Morris <danielle.morris@ledgercorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent tail-latency spikes affecting Ledger Checkout — renewal conversation

Thanks for flagging this, Danielle — and sorry for the disruption. We took an initial look at the incident logs you sent.

Quick summary from our side:
- We can see the same tail events correlated to bursty tokenization patterns + a small percentage of requests routing to a suboptimal model variant during peak windows.
- Short-term mitigations we can deploy within 48–72 hours: stricter routing policies to avoid the older variant, temporary prefix KV caching tuning, and emergency circuit-breaker thresholds to prevent error amplification.

For the renewal/commercial side, I propose the following:
1) A 30-day premium trial (priority allocation + stricter SLOs for tail latency) so you can validate at-scale.
2) A one-time service credit (we'll propose 15% of the May invoice) while we run the trial.
3) If trial metrics meet the agreed SLOs, we'll move to a premium addendum with defined uptime and latency commitments and an expedited onramp to Dedicated capacity if you choose.

I'm attaching a short analysis we produced and a draft addendum (proposed-premium-addendum_v1.pdf) for your legal team.

Can Marissa and Ben weigh in on the ops plan and the proposed commercial credit? Also, Danielle — what times work for a 30–45 minute call today or tomorrow?

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Morris <danielle.morris@ledgercorp.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent tail-latency spikes affecting Ledger Checkout — remediation plan

On Tue, May 11, 2027 at 12:03 PM Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> For the renewal/commercial side, I propose the following...

Hi Danielle — Marissa from Customer Reliability/CS here. Thanks for the detailed logs. I want to be explicit about the ops path so expectations are clear:

Proposed technical timeline (ops):
- Day 0–2: Apply routing policy change + KV cache tuning (no code changes required).
- Day 3–10: Run high-fidelity traffic test window during a controlled peak (we'll coordinate a mirror test with your staging traffic).
- Day 11–30: Pilot on priority routing (measured by INF-9276 test suite; we'll share dashboards).

Success metrics for the pilot:
- 95th percentile tail latency < 220 ms during peak windows
- error rate reduction of 60% vs the May 9 spike window
- cross-validated traces in our shared dashboard

Commercial accommodations: Redwood will provide the 30-day premium trial and the 15% May credit Olga proposed. If pilot fails to meet the metrics, we'll extend the trial by two weeks at no charge and provide a one-time renewal credit to make up measurable conversion loss.

I'll own the pilot runbook and the dashboard. Suggest call tomorrow 11:00–11:45 PT to align.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: procurement@ledgercorp.com
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@ledgercorp.com>, Danielle Morris <danielle.morris@ledgercorp.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent tail-latency spikes affecting Ledger Checkout — renewal conversation (procurement input)

Thanks — procurement here. A few asks before we can accept the trial/credit proposal:
- Please provide the draft SLA addendum in DocuSign-ready format and call out exact SLO language and remedies.
- We need confirmation on data residency, audit logs (retention 13 months), and whether any Dedicated-hosted option will require an MSA amendment.
- Legal prefers a 60-day review window for any addendum; can you expedite a clean DocuSign link?

Please cc legal@ledgercorp.com on the final doc and include the HubSpot deal ID (LC-4521) on all paperwork.

Procurement will also need the invoice credit line shown separately in the May invoice.

Procurement Team
LedgerCorp
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Morris <danielle.morris@ledgercorp.com>, procurement@ledgercorp.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent tail-latency spikes affecting Ledger Checkout — renewal / MAP and next steps

Thanks all — summary / mutual action plan (MAP) below so we have a single source of truth: 

1) Ops fixes (Olga/Marissa) — ETA: 72 hours for routing + KV tuning; mirror test scheduled for 2027-05-18; pilot run 2027-05-19 to 2027-06-17.
2) Commercial (Ben/Olga) — Redwood to issue 15% credit on May invoice; Ben will circulate a DocuSign-ready addendum with explicit SLO language and remedies by 2027-05-17. Link will include data-residency and log-retention clauses per procurement.
3) Legal/Procurement (LedgerCorp) — 60-day review noted; we'll ask for a prioritized review and follow-up by 2027-05-20.
4) Success metrics — 95th percentile tail latency < 220 ms; 60% reduction in spike error rate. Verified via shared dashboard (INF-9276).

Action items: 
- Ben Carter: prepare DocuSign addendum and commercial summary (due 2027-05-17).
- Marissa Cole: finalize pilot runbook and dashboard, confirm mirror test details (due 2027-05-17).
- Olga Petrov: schedule the executive call and share the HubSpot deal link + JIRA ticket.

I've attached the latency analysis and draft addendum for initial review (latency-analysis-may2027.pdf, proposed-premium-addendum_v1.pdf). Ben, please follow up with the DocuSign link and the itemized invoice credit line.

Call scheduled: 2027-05-17 11:00 PT (30 minutes) — calendar invite to follow.

Thanks — looking forward to getting LedgerCorp back to baseline and moving the renewal forward.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
